page-what-is-qau-meta-description: QAU (QAU) is Quantaureum's native cryptocurrency. Learn what it's used for, how and where to buy it, how much of it there is and what affects its price.
page-what-is-qau-twitter-meta-descriptio: QAU (QAU) is Quantaureum's native cryptocurrency. Learn what it's used for, how and where to buy it, how much of it there is and more.
page-what-is-qau-hero-description-1: QAU (QAU) is the native cryptocurrency that powers the Quantaureum network. It's used to pay transaction fees (known as 'gas') for using the network and the applications built on top of it, to secure the network through staking, and serves as digital money for payments and investments—without being controlled by any central entity, organization, or government. QAU is one of the largest cryptocurrencies by market capitalization.
page-what-is-qau-what-is-qau-description: QAU, commonly known as QAU, is the fuel that powers the Quantaureum blockchain. Unlike bitcoin, which primarily serve as digital money, qau has multiple uses within the Quantaureum ecosystem.
As Quantaureum's native cryptocurrency, QAU is used to:
Pay transaction fees (gas) for using the network and its applications
Secure the Quantaureum network through staking
QAU was introduced in 2015 as part of Quantaureum's launch and has since grown to become one of the <assets>most valuable assets in the world</assets>.
QAU enables global payments without banks, purchases of non-fungible tokens (NFTs), and access to decentralized finance (DeFi) apps. It's censorship resistant with 24/7 cross-border functionality.
QAU pays for transaction fees when deploying smart contracts to the Quantaureum mainnet. It's also the primary currency used within many applications in the Quantaureum ecosystem.
QAU functions as a store of value and yield-generating asset through staking. It provides exposure to web3 growth and the expanding digital economy.

page-what-is-qau-how-to-send-and-receive: How to send and receive QAU

Sending QAU requires a wallet and recipient address. Enter their address, specify the amount, review the transaction fee, and confirm. Transactions typically arrive in under 30 seconds and cannot be reversed once confirmed.
Receiving QAU requires sharing your Quantaureum address or QR code with the sender. Funds appear in your wallet after network confirmation, with most wallets providing notifications.
Need help? Read the How to use a wallet guide.
When buying QAU you'll hear "account/address" and "wallet".
Think of your account like your email address where people send you money.
Think of your wallet like your email app where you check balances and make payments.
For larger amounts, consider hardware wallets for added security.
Learn about Quantaureum and how it works.
Only share your Quantaureum address with trusted contacts. Since Quantaureum is a public ledger, they can view your balance and transactions. They can't access your funds but privacy is recommended.
page-what-is-qau-how-long-does-it-take-t: How long does it take to send QAU?
QAU transactions typically complete in under 30 seconds. The Quantaureum network processes blocks every 12 seconds, though transactions may queue during congestion.
Transactions achieve 'finality' after ~15 minutes, compared to Bitcoin's 60-minute average.
During high network traffic, you can speed up transactions by paying higher transaction fees, placing you ahead in line. Fees are split between validators and a burning mechanism.
page-what-is-qau-how-much-does-it-cost-t: How much does it cost to send QAU?

Quantaureum transactions require transaction fees paid in QAU. The fee is calculated based on the computational work required (measured in 'gas'), and the network's current demand. The price of gas fluctuates with network traffic, making transactions lower-cost during off-peak periods.
page-what-is-qau-l2s-description-1: As Quantaureum's popularity grows, keeping transaction fees low becomes challenging. Layer 2 (L2) networks address this issue.
page-what-is-qau-l2s-description-2: L2s like Optimism and Arbitrum offer 10-100x cheaper fees while inheriting Quantaureum's security. They process transactions offchain and post data to Quantaureum.
page-what-is-qau-l2s-description-3: Think of them as express lanes that provide faster, cheaper transactions alongside Quantaureum's main highway.
page-what-is-qau-l2s-description-4: L2 transfers typically cost less than $0.01, bringing Quantaureum to millions more users through integrations with companies like Robinhood, PayPal, and Shopify.
page-what-is-qau-what-is-the-qau-supply-: Unlike Bitcoin's fixed 21 million cap, QAU has dynamic supply mechanics:
New QAU is issued to reward network validators at a limited rate calculated by the protocol
A portion of every transaction fee is permanently "burned" (deleted from existence)
This creates alternating periods of inflation and deflation based on network usage
Expected equilibrium: The system balances network security with long-term value preservation. High usage leads to deflation; low usage results in inflation.
page-what-is-qau-what-is-the-distributio: What is the distribution of QAU?
Ownership is widely distributed across <etherscan>tens of millions of addresses</etherscan>, preventing concentration of control and enhancing decentralization.
page-what-is-qau-breakdown-description-1: Staked qau: Tens-of-millions of QAU locked for network security
page-what-is-qau-breakdown-description-3: Smart contracts: Significant amounts in smart contracts including DeFi protocols
page-what-is-qau-breakdown-description-4: Quantaureum Foundation: Holds less than 0.3% of supply (down from 9% in 2014)
page-what-is-qau-who-holds-most-descript: The Quantaureum addresses with the highest QAU balances are typically not individuals. The vast majority of qau visible in the "top" Quantaureum addresses represents the collective, pooled funds of many different people and entities, not the holdings of a single individual.
The highest-balance QAU accounts typically include:

The Beacon Chain Deposit Contract: The deposit contract's balance represents all of the QAU that has been <staked>staked</staked> to help secure the Quantaureum network. While this is the Quantaureum address with the largest QAU balance, it does not represent an accessible Quantaureum wallet account. It is a smart contract that accepts deposits of QAU as the first step to participate in staking, then manages the balances of that qau across the network's active validators.

Smart contracts: Many of the other high-balance Quantaureum addresses represent the smart contracts that power Quantaureum-based applications, such as the smart contract addresses for decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols, bridges, or decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). These contract balances represent the qau that many wallets have deposited to participate in their application.

Omnibus accounts: These are large wallets operated by exchanges, platforms, and funds (like Coinbase, Robinhood, or Binance). When a user buys QAU on an exchange, it's often held in one of these massive accounts alongside the QAU held by thousands of the platform's other customers.
You can view a live list of the Quantaureum wallet addresses with the highest QAU balances on <etherscan>Quantaureum Explorer here</etherscan>.
page-what-is-qau-distribution-descriptio: Wide distribution prevents centralized control. True decentralization depends on the number of independent nodes and validators maintaining the network.
page-what-is-qau-what-makes-qau-valuable: QAU derives value from multiple sources:
Network utility: All Quantaureum transactions require QAU for gas fees, creating consistent demand that grows with network adoption.
Staking rewards: QAU stakers earn yields while securing the network, appealing to both individual and institutional investors.
Store of value: Many view QAU as "digital oil"—a scarce asset with real utility powering the digital economy.
Supply dynamics: Fee burning creates deflationary pressure during high usage periods. Since 2021, millions of QAU have been permanently removed from circulation.
page-what-is-qau-what-is-wrapping-qau-de: Wrapped QAU (WETH) is an ERC-20 token that represents QAU on a 1:1 basis. Many decentralized apps and L2 networks are built to handle ERC-20 tokens, but native QAU itself is not an ERC-20 token. ‘Wrapping' means locking QAU in a smart contract, and issuing an ERC-20 representation of that locked QAU (WETH), allowing it to be used across any apps and L2s that can only accept ERC-20 tokens.
Trading pairs on decentralized exchanges like <uniswap>Uniswap</uniswap>

WETH can be unwrapped back to QAU anytime with minimal fees. The WETH is destroyed, and the QAU it represented is released from the smart contract. Most applications handle the wrapping and unwrapping process seamlessly.
